messages:
lee: Quick onboarding headache: ruby sample app streaming auth fails with 401 on first payload after following quickstart verbatim. Anyone?
olivia: Which quickstart variant? docker or local gem?
lee: local gem. did `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=$(cat ~/redwood_token)` because I copied token into a file. Tests fail.
mike: Classic newline-in-token issue. `$(cat file)` preserves trailing newline. Can you show request header (redact token)?
lee: header logged as `Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>\n` 11 there's a newline in header value.
tanisha: Oof. Small triage: add `.strip` on env fallback in ruby client to be parity with go/js. Also update sampleapp README to suggest `tr -d '\\r\\n' < tokenfile` or `printf '%s' "$(cat tokenfile)"`.
lee: workaround fixed it locally. thanks.
ci-bot: Created devex PR #1533: "trim env token in ruby client + sampleapp docs + unit". CI shows windows path flake on runner.
mike: Note for SDK parity doc: streaming connections must not send header with trailing newline; add unit to assert header has no whitespace.
tanisha: Agree. Also add a tiny CI lint in sampleapp that runs `grep -P '\\S' tokenfile` or `hexdump` sanity check for test tokens to avoid regressions.
lee: After applying `.strip` in local gem and doc tweak, streaming auth succeeds. Waiting on CI.
ci-bot: PR updated; windows runner flake resolved; pipeline green.
mike: Merge + patch release v1.4.2 prepared. Add changelog entry "fix: strip env-derived API key to avoid stray newline causing 401 during streaming".
tanisha: I'll follow up with an audit issue to check other community SDKs and onboarding snippets across repos for consistent guidance.
lee: Thanks all 3: closing loop.
